blocks.content: If we put all these pieces together, the posterior density for draws from a normal with unknown mean and variance is obtained as follows. First, we write the joint prior by conditioning on the variance, $$ p(\mu,\sigma^{2})=p(\mu\mid\sigma^{2})\cdot p(\sigma^{2}) $$ As above, we assume a scaled inverse chi-square distribution for the variance and, conditioned on the variance, a Gaussian prior for the mean with hyperparameters of $ \mu_0 $ and $ \sigma^2/\kappa_0 $, namely, $$ \sigma^{2}\sim\chi_{\nu_{0},\sigma_{0}^{2}}^{-2}\qquad\mathrm{a n d}\qquad\mu\mid\sigma^{2}\sim\mathrm{N}\left(\mu_{0},\frac{\sigma^{2}}{\kappa_{0}}\right) $$
